turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Alright, thanks. Ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Went to bed around 11, but I was up at 6 this morning, so — do the math, it wasn't a lot. Some weeks the shift schedule doesn't care what time I "meant" to sleep.
Approximately how many hours do you think you actually slept last night? And would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Probably five to six hours, if I'm being generous with the math. I'd say it was decent, not great — I got interrupted around 3am by a work text, but I fell back asleep fine, so it's not like I was staring at the ceiling all night.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed?
Last thing before bed I usually just watch some TV — low volume, kind of like background noise until I doze off. Didn't do anything special last night.
Why do you usually choose to watch TV as your last activity before going to sleep?
Just habit at this point — it's mindless, keeps the room from being dead silent, and I don't have to think about it. Doesn't require any effort, which is kind of the point after a long shift.
Thanks for explaining that. Over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

Factors like the work text at 3am waking me up, and the rotating shift schedule messing with when I actually go to bed — that's probably the biggest one. Other than that, not much has changed on my end.
Is that rotating shift schedule and getting work messages at odd hours pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently in the last little while?

Pretty typical, yeah. The shift rotation's been going on for a couple years now, so I'm used to it. The 3am texts happen more than I'd like — comes with coordinating trucks that don't care what time it is — but nothing's really changed lately, just the usual grind.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Not really happy, no — I get by, but waking up once or twice a night's just the norm for me at this point. It's not the end of the world, functional over great, I guess. If the shift didn't jump around so much I'd probably sleep better, but that's the job.
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Seven to nine hours sounds nice in theory, but with the shift jumping around I'm lucky to get seven most weeks — some weeks it's closer to six. I don't stress about hitting a number though, I just try to feel decent when I'm up. If I chased nine hours on a 6am week I'd have to go to bed at like 8pm, and that's not happening.
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

Honestly, the shift changing every week or two is the main thing that makes it hard — my body never fully settles into one bedtime. What makes it easier is when the schedule's steady for a stretch, or when work doesn't blow up my phone overnight.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

Yeah, honestly — the 3am thing tonight was because of that. I keep it on the nightstand for work reasons, so if it buzzes I'm gonna look at it, and then I'm scrolling for a few minutes before I realize what I'm doing. Not proud of it, but when your phone's basically a work radio you can't really leave it in another room.
That makes sense. Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
Not really, no. I'm on there sometimes, but it's more of a lunch-break scroll thing than a bedtime habit — once the phone's on the nightstand it's just for texts, not doom-scrolling feeds.

Thanks for explaining that. Now a quick question about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots (like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps)? If yes, what do you mainly use them for?

Not really, no. Wouldn't trust it to tell me anything about my own body that I don't already know from just living in it — I mostly just use it for boring stuff, like drafting an email or looking something up quick.
Since you do use them a bit, do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all since you began using AI chatbots regularly?

Nah, not really. I don't really use them enough for that, and definitely not around bedtime — like I said, it's more a "help me word this email" thing at lunch than anything touching my sleep. My sleep habits are messed with by my schedule, not by chatbots.
Thanks for clarifying that. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

Honestly? Getting the phone off the nightstand, or at least on silent for anything but the emergency line. Everything else I can live with — the shift work I've made peace with, but that 3am buzz-and-scroll thing is the one habit that's actually optional.
Given your work and daily responsibilities, do you think making that change with your phone would be doable? Why or why not?

"Yeah, doable — silent mode's not exactly a heavy lift. I've already got emergency contacts starred, so it's really just flipping one setting instead of leaving the whole thing wide open. No real excuse other than laziness, honestly."

Thanks for explaining that. Now a few background questions—feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.

What is your age, your profession, your country of birth, and your current country of residence?
Age's 52. Logistics coordinator at a warehouse — I move boxes around on a schedule, basically. Born and still living in the same country, so nothing exotic there.

Thanks for sharing that. A couple of quick follow-ups, if you’re comfortable:

Which country is that, and is there anything else you’d like to add about your sleep or your schedule that we haven’t talked about yet?
